content.comment_body: Hello, can someone help me with a problem detecting [product_name] hardware? I've directly connected an Ethernet cable to the device but can't detect it. This issue started after I installed [product_name] software on the same PC. I understand the IP can be retrieved from the display, but what if the device doesn't have a display? I've tried entering the IP in [product_name] management software to test the connection, but detection still fails. Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you.

You can try transferring a program, which should open a window in the software. In this window, click the icon with circular blue arrows. The software will then attempt to find devices automatically. If devices are found, their IP address and subnet mask will be shown in a table.

Hi, generally, [product_name] management software handles Ethernet automatically, but note some restrictions: 1) The software must run with administrator rights. 2) If you manually set the PC Ethernet IP and it matches the one for [product_name] (PG/PC interface), you might have conflicts. Try opening the PG/PC interface and choosing a different Ethernet adapter for [product_name]. Switch back when needed, or add another Ethernet adapter. Having two adapters—one for each application—sometimes causes issues because Windows can't always handle multiple interfaces well. It's best to use dedicated adapters and fixed IP addresses for each application. Hope this helps.

It's mostly about network setup. Go to your PC's network and sharing center, select local area connection, then properties, and double-click IPv4. Choose 'obtain an IP address automatically' and 'obtain DNS server address automatically,' then click OK. If this doesn't resolve the issue, run the network troubleshooter. The latest version of [product_name] management software can automatically detect compatible hardware.

Possible reasons include a bad network cable or incorrect IP configuration on either the PC or device. Solutions: If the device is new, use the default IP address, subnet mask, and gateway in the PC's network settings. You can use IP detection tools if your device has a preset IP, or take advantage of the automatic detection features in [product_name] management software.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulties detecting [product_name] hardware with the management software, especially after installing other [company_name] software on their Windows PC. Manual IP entry does not solve the issue, and root causes discussed include IP address conflicts, required admin rights, and proper Ethernet configuration. Participants display uncertainty regarding networking prerequisites and process clarity, often due to limited network configuration experience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect seamless, automated detection of [product_name] hardware by its management software, with an easy network setup and reliable compatibility between various [company_name] programs on a single PC. Users desire a straightforward workflow regardless of device version or the presence of a display.
